archetype: Organic Precision meets Swiss Performance Athletics (Archetype 2: Tactical Sports Performance paired with Architectural Biomechanics)
design_vision: A luxury, minimalist tennis laboratory aesthetic. Inspired by Swiss editorial design, Swiss Timing precision, and professional kinetic capture labs. Stark clean porcelain white backgrounds with surgical tennis court green (#15803D / #166534 / #22C55E) accents, precise 1px architectural hairline borders, technical monospace data points, and deep charcoal slate text. No cluttered gradients or neon gimmicks; raw photographic presence where the athlete dominates the viewport with interactive biometric overlay telemetry.

movement_timeline.description: Selectable 7-phase sequence spanning the full stroke cycle

phases.label: 01. Ready Position
phases.cue: Wide athletic base, racket head up, chest relaxed.

phases.label: 02. Unit Turn
phases.cue: Shoulders rotate 90° as one unit; non-dominant hand tracks the ball.

phases.label: 03. Kinetic Load
phases.cue: Back leg flexion, kinetic energy stored in hip coil, racket drops below ball line.

phases.label: 04. Forward Swing
phases.cue: Hips fire first, elbow leads into slot, wrist lags naturally (racket drop).

phases.label: 05. Contact Point
phases.cue: Ball struck comfortably out in front, stable wrist, eyes locked through point.

phases.label: 06. Follow Through
phases.cue: Windshield wiper motion over opposite shoulder, torso rotated open.

phases.label: 07. Dynamic Recovery
phases.cue: Outside leg pushes back toward center hash, split step reset.

hotspots_data.label: Head & Eye Tracking
hotspots_data.role: Anchors balance. Head must remain completely still through the contact zone for 0.2s post-strike to prevent frame mishits.
hotspots_data.mistake: Looking up early toward the opponent court before the ball clears the strings, dropping the racket angle.
hotspots_data.drill: Keep gaze fixed on the empty impact airspace until follow-through touches opposite shoulder.

hotspots_data.label: Shoulder Complex & Rotational Axis
hotspots_data.role: Creates angular momentum via rotational torque. Left shoulder pulls through while right shoulder drives upward.
hotspots_data.mistake: Passive torso rotation where the arm swings alone without kinetic shoulder involvement ('arming the ball').
hotspots_data.drill: Shadow swings focusing on pointing the chest at the fence post-finish.

hotspots_data.label: Elbow Slot & Extension
hotspots_data.role: Tucked comfortably 4-6 inches from rib cage in slot position, extending outward toward target line during acceleration.
hotspots_data.mistake: Elbow jammed tight against hip or hyper-straightened during backswing, killing topspin whip.
hotspots_data.drill: Towel under armpit drill: keep a microfiber towel pinched until initial forward racket acceleration.

hotspots_data.label: Wrist Lag & Radial Stability
hotspots_data.role: Lags behind handle naturally during forward drive, snaps into stable contact position without active 'flicking'.
hotspots_data.mistake: Active loose flicking trying to manually create topspin, leading to tendonitis and errant spray.
hotspots_data.drill: L-shape freeze drill: maintain firm 90-degree wrist extension at address.

hotspots_data.label: Hip Coil & Core Uncoiling
hotspots_data.role: The primary engine of ground power. Right hip uncoils first, pulling torso, arm, and racket through the kinetic chain.
hotspots_data.mistake: Hips remaining static or square to net throughout the entire backswing.
hotspots_data.drill: Medicine ball rotational toss against wall to program hip-initiated power sequence.

hotspots_data.label: Knee Bend & Vertical Drive
hotspots_data.role: Right knee flexes to approximately 110° to drop center of gravity and push explosively into the court.
hotspots_data.mistake: Standing upright with stiff knees, forcing the upper body to compensate for lack of lift.
hotspots_data.drill: Low-to-high cone touch: touch a low cone before initiating every shadow stroke.

hotspots_data.label: Feet & Stance Anchor
hotspots_data.role: Semi-open stance anchoring back foot 45° to baseline for rapid recovery and torque distribution.
hotspots_data.mistake: Crossed-over closed stance on aggressive balls that locks the hips and forces arming.
hotspots_data.drill: Figure-8 footwork around two cones placed 4 feet apart on the baseline.

hotspots_data.label: Racquet Face Angle & Path
hotspots_data.role: Slightly closed face (8-12°) upon descent, brushing up 45° across the back-outside quadrant of the ball for heavy topspin.
hotspots_data.mistake: Open racquet face causing balls to launch deep beyond baseline or erratic high floaters.
hotspots_data.drill: Fence brush exercise: shadow swing along chain link fence keeping face parallel to fence.

hotspots_data.label: Ball & Contact Point
hotspots_data.role: Struck 12-18 inches in front of front hip at waist-to-rib level with sweet-spot alignment.
hotspots_data.mistake: Letting ball get behind the body plane, losing all kinetic leverage and spray control.
hotspots_data.drill: Drop-feed hit from static hold: partner drops ball 1.5 ft in front; player freezes at contact.

accessibility_and_testing.test_id_rules: All interactive buttons, tabs, level pills, timeline steps, and hotspot markers MUST have explicit data-testid attributes
accessibility_and_testing.color_contrast: All text satisfies WCAG AA (Minimum 4.5:1 ratio on light porcelain background). Muted slate text uses #4B5563 or #1E2922
accessibility_and_testing.keyboard_nav: Hotspots can be cycled via Tab and activated with Enter/Space; Left/Right arrow keys navigate the 7-phase timeline

instructions_to_main_agent: Build a complete, responsive React application with clean navigation between the Homepage ('/') and the Forehand Technique Lab ('/forehand').
Use pure Tailwind CSS utilities combined with custom typography classes. Avoid generic default templates.
Import Google Fonts 'Plus Jakarta Sans', 'Cabinet Grotesk', and 'JetBrains Mono' inside src/index.css before Tailwind imports.

On the Forehand page, render the athlete image inside a responsive relative container and place all 9 circular hotspot markers using precise absolute percentage coordinates so they align intuitively with anatomical areas (Head, Shoulder, Elbow, Wrist, Hip, Knee, Feet, Racquet, Contact Point).
Ensure each hotspot marker displays its index number or icon, pulses subtly, and updates the adjacent Biomechanics Telemetry Card with active role, common mistakes, and level-specific drills.
Implement the 7-phase kinetic timeline underneath the player image (Ready, Unit Turn, Load, Forward Swing, Contact, Follow Through, Recovery) allowing players to scrub or click through stroke phases.
Implement the UTR Level Selector (UTR 1-2, UTR 2-4, UTR 4-6) on both pages to customize the coaching advice from fundamental stability to high-rpm topspin mechanics.
Include high-polish micro-interactions: quick category filters, level switching, toast feedback for drill saving, and smooth tab transitions.
All interactive elements must carry unambiguous data-testid attributes.
